title: The Beginning
text:
Towards the end of my 12th standard, Computer Science stopped being another school subject and became something I genuinely wanted to understand.

That curiosity led me to Harvard's CS50P.

title: Learning How To Think
text:
CS50P wasn't simply about Python.

It taught me
• Problem solving
• Logical thinking
• Breaking difficult problems into manageable pieces
• Patience
• Confidence

Completing it entirely on my own became one of the defining moments of my early learning journey.

title: Discovering Intelligence
text:
After learning programming, a new question appeared.

"How do machines actually think?"

That question naturally led me to Harvard's CS50AI.

Instead of another programming course, it introduced me to the foundations of Artificial Intelligence.

Search.
Optimization.
Machine Learning.
Neural Networks.
Reasoning.

It wasn't another certificate.

It changed the questions I was asking.

title: Going Deeper
text:
Curiosity naturally expanded into Machine Learning and Deep Learning.

I completed Deep Learning for Computer Vision with TensorFlow.

Then explored JAX.
Then PyTorch.

Every framework became another way of understanding the same ideas.

Instead of attaching myself to one ecosystem, I became interested in understanding the concepts beneath them.

title: Building
text:
Learning slowly transformed into building.

Hackathons.
Backend systems.
Artificial Intelligence.
OpenEnv.
Collaborative projects.

Every project became another opportunity to understand how real systems are built.

title: Still Becoming
text:
I don't define myself by a framework.
Or a programming language.

I enjoy exploring ideas.

Whether that's
AI.
Distributed Systems.
Backend Engineering.
Cinema.
Books.
Music.
Design.

Every subject offers another perspective.

I'm simply trying to understand the world a little better than yesterday.
